title: Speciality Restaurants Ltd - 534425 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q1 FY27 same-store sales grew 11.35% and gross margin rose 1.2pp to 71.1%, with management declining to give a INR600 crore revenue target.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 as the company's 20th consecutive profitable quarter, with same-store sales growth of 11.35% on a like-for-like basis versus Q1 FY26. Gross margin improved to 71.1% from 69.9%, attributed to portion control, reduced inefficiencies and vendor negotiations, despite inflation. Management said July was extremely good versus last July and early August trends were good across dine-in and delivery. Management declined to commit to a INR600 crore revenue figure but said Q3 would be a good quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Grew over last year per presentation

financial_highlights.value: 8-9% from existing food-driven stores; 40% in wetland restaurant

financial_highlights.metric: Cash balance (as referenced by analyst from last quarter)
financial_highlights.change: Management expects to maintain by year end

segments.name: Oriental (Mainland China, Gong, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Bizarre Asia)
segments.commentary: Management says Oriental is sub-50% of revenue and remains the biggest contributor. Price tiers: Gong INR 2,500, Mainland China INR 1,250, Asia Kitchen INR 1,050-1,100, Haka (delivery-first) INR 600 per person.

segments.name: Italian (Siciliana)
segments.commentary: Positioned as a growth engine; liquor is about 25% of sales at Siciliana. Paired with Asia Kitchen in mall deals to improve revenue-to-effort ratio.

segments.name: QSR (Walters Burgers, Sweet Bengal)
segments.commentary: Walters has 3 principal stores and 2 cloud kitchens; management says revenue grew about 300% from the prior quarter with one new store added. Plans 10-15 Walters stores this year and 5 new stores by year-end. Sweet Bengal's hero product is Kheer Kadam; shelf life extended to 30 days.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to confirm whether the company would cross INR600 crore in revenue, but said it is working for good percentage growth, with Q3 expected to be a good quarter.
Company plans 8-10 restaurant openings in FY27 plus 10-15 Walters QSR stores; management denied a 32-store plan.
Cash expected to be maintained at around the INR162 crore level by year-end, with capex funded from internal cash generation.
Gross margin historically held within plus or minus 50bps; price increases are used tactically to offset raw-material pressure.
Joint development of the Odisha F&B plot (Speciality Hotels India Pvt Ltd) expected to complete by FY27 year-end; company to hold about 34% of the demerged entity.
capex_capacity: Plan of 8-10 restaurant openings per financial year plus Walters smaller-format QSR units (10-15 this year); 5 new Walters stores by end of this year.
Gong openings planned in Vasant Kunj (Delhi) and a second Pune outlet; Gong currently in Pune and Bandra (Mumbai).
Mainland China renovation programme ongoing ('Mainland China 2'); at least five renovated units have added visible bars.
Kitchen conversion from gas ranges to induction for a hybrid gas/electric setup, after gas shortages; 11 cloud kitchens in portfolio.
Management said trained manpower, not locations or capital, is the biggest constraint on expansion.
demand_pricing: Management said July 2026 was extremely good versus last July, and the first 7-10 days of August were good for both dine-in and delivery.
Weekday demand is supported by tactical offers, set meals, corporate lunches and delivery combos; management said the weekend/weekday split is still the same as before, about 45:55.
Service charge was withdrawn from 7 June; a price increase was taken to offset it.

Delivery growth was attributed to new formats (Walters, Sweet Bengal, Haka), marketing, tactical discounts and in-house delivery staff; management said delivery is lower-margin but gives operating leverage above revenue thresholds.
Shravan and Ganpati cyclicality was described as having limited impact overall, with a slight Western India impact during Ganpati.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cross INR600 crore in revenue with about 15 new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a revenue target, citing a positive trend and a focus on good percentage growth, with Q3 expected to be strong.

qa_highlights.question: How was margin expanded despite cost pressure, including gas shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Rate contracts for six months or a full year, pipe-gas supply in Mumbai, and a shift from gas to induction helped; portion-size efficiencies offset inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the delivery mix growth deliberate, and does it hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is driven by consumer demand and new formats, not a deliberate push. Dine-in grew from INR 71 crore to INR 81 crore; AOV is claimed to be among the highest in dine-in brands.

qa_highlights.question: How many stores are planned, and what are the constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: 8-10 restaurants per year plus 10-15 Walters; trained manpower is the main constraint, not locations or capital.

qa_highlights.question: Will price increases be used to protect gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically gross margin held within plus or minus 50bps; tactical price increases are used to offset raw-material and other cost inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Speciality Hotels (Odisha plot) status?
qa_highlights.answer: Joint development is progressing and expected to complete by FY27 year-end; the company will hold about 34% of the demerged entity post completion.

risks_watch: Gross margin sustainability under rising input, staff, power and licensing costs; price increases may be needed.
Trained manpower shortage may limit the pace of restaurant and Walters expansion.
Shift toward delivery (29% of revenue), which carries higher variable costs and tactical discounting.
Brand rationalisation: older brands to be phased out; Bizarre Asia format's future is unclear.
Liquor sales ramp-up targets (8-9% of revenue from food-driven stores) depend on renovations and contracts.
Cash balance guidance (about INR162 crore maintained) relies on internal cash generation for capex.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, same-store sales and near-term demand, but evasive on the INR600 crore revenue question and on store-count numbers. Management was also defensive when challenged on delivery mix and the brand portfolio.
